title: Bibliographic Data
description: Tests models on extracting structured entries (author, title, publisher, place, year, pages, cross-references) from the pages of a printed 1961 bibliography of the philosophy of history.

source.collection: History and Theory, Beiheft 1 (1961), via JSTOR

versions.summary: ground truth checked against the scans and conformed to the response schema (transcription errors, six missing entries, entries 146–148 unnested, `relation` as the reviewed `id`, notes and years as printed); `prompt_v2.txt` for new tests; entries aligned in page order instead of by position; a response nested under a wrapper key is unwrapped; a response that cannot be parsed is scored as a miss; all stored runs re-scored
initial versioned state, when the card was introduced; same content as 0.10.1
per-field comparison recorded with each answer; scores unchanged
an answer that cannot be parsed is left out of the average instead of scored as a miss
a run with no scored object scores 0 instead of failing
a failed object is left out of the average instead of stopping the run
answers are parsed by the API client instead of the benchmark; failed requests stop the run again
numbers and strings compared as text, so a number matches the same digits given as a string
requests that fail are saved as empty answers and scored as misses
the prompt states the page number instead of a literal `{page_number}`
schema rebuilt with pydantic: `relation` and `reprint` become strings, empty defaults become null
`metadata` fields no longer scored; answers given as a list are accepted; two ground-truth files made valid JSON
three pages added (page_3 to page_5); `issued` asked for as a string
